subject: Setting up two types of layers in micro_ functions

messages.author: d16378cf7bf5eca2
messages.subject: Setting up two types of layers in micro_ functions
parts:
Good day Mike,

I'm using microclimate(), micro_era5() and micro_ncep() functions to predict mussel body temperatures. I could set two layers (mussel between 0-5 cm and granite below) to be used by microclimate():

```
DEP <- c(0, 2.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200)
Numtyps <- 2  # set 2 types of layer: 0-5cm = mussel and 5+ = granite (see below)
Nodes <- matrix(data = 0, nrow = 10, ncol = doynum)
Nodes[1, 1:doynum] <- 10
soilprops <- matrix(data = 0, nrow = 10, ncol = 5)
# set mussel layer (0-5 cm):
soilprops[1:3, 1] <- BulkDensity <- Density <- 1.086 # mussel flesh (g/cm3)
soilprops[1:3, 2] <- SatWater <- 0.95 # mussel flesh, typically close to 1
soilprops[1:3, 3] <- Thcond <- 0.5681 # mussel flesh (W/m-C)
soilprops[1:3, 4] <- SpecHeat <- 3496.3 # mussel flesh (J/kg-C)
soilprops[1:3, 5] <- Density
# set granite layer (+5-200 cm):
soilprops[4:10, 1] <- BulkDensity_rock <- Density_rock <- 2.7 # granite (g/cm3)
soilprops[4:10, 2] <- SatWater_rock <- 0.34 # weathered granite
soilprops[4:10, 3] <- Thcond_rock <- 2.99 # weathered granite with high porosity under saturated conditions (W/m-C)
soilprops[4:10, 4] <- SpecHeat_rock <- 800 # weathered granite under saturated conditions (J/kg-C)
soilprops[4:10, 5] <- Density_rock
soilinit <- rep(tannul, 20)
soiltype <- 0 # rock
PE <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype, 4],19)
KS <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype, 6],19)
BB <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype, 5],19)
BD <- rep(BulkDensity_rock, 19) # granite layer
BD[1:5] <- BulkDensity # mussel layer (0-5cm)
DD <- rep(Density_rock, 19) # granite layer
DD[1:5] <- Density # mussel layer (0-5cm)
```

But I don't know how "soilprops" is specified in micro_ functions. Do these functions currently assume there is only one homogeneous layer?

Best regards,

Jonathan

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Setting up two types of layers in micro_ functions
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

That's easy kind of easy in that you just feed in the PE, KS, BD and BB directly as vectors (of 19 values) and the same for Thcond, Density, BulkDensity and SpecHeat (10 values, 1 per depth). However I had to make a tweak to get this to work properly so you'll need to get the latest version from github.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Setting up two types of layers in micro_ functions
parts:
Hi Mike,

Ok sounds good. I’ve updated NicheMapR from github (devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR')) and set the two layers as follows:

Thcond_mussel=0.5681 # mussel flesh (W/m-C)
BulkDensity_mussel=Density_mussel=1.086 # mussel flesh (g/cm3)
SpecHeat_mussel=3496.3 # mussel flesh (J/kg-C)

Thcond_granite=2.99 # weathered granite (W/m-C)
BulkDensity_granite=Density_granite=2.7 # weathered granite (g/cm3)
SpecHeat_granite=800 # weathered granite (J/kg-C)

Thcond=c(rep(Thcond_mussel, 3), rep(Thcond_granite, 7))
BulkDensity=Density=c(rep(BulkDensity_mussel, 3), rep(BulkDensity_granite, 7))
SpecHeat=c(rep(SpecHeat_mussel, 3), rep(SpecHeat_granite, 7))

PE <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[0, 4],19) # force rock properties
KS <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[0, 6],19) # force rock properties
BB <- rep(CampNormTbl9_1[0, 5],19) # force rock properties
BD <- rep(BulkDensity_granite, 19) # granite layer (>5-200cm)
BD[1:5] <- BulkDensity_mussel # mussel layer (0-5cm)
DD <- rep(Density_granite, 19) # granite layer (>5-200cm)
DD[1:5] <- Density_mussel # mussel layer (0-5cm)

But I get an error message saying that only the first values for 'Thcond', 'Density', and 'SpecHeat' are being used:

Warning messages:
1: In if (Thcond < 0) { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
2: In if (Density < 0) { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
3: In if (SpecHeat < 0) { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
4: In microclima::microclimaforNMR(lat = longlat[2], long = longlat[1],  :
  Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in EET
5: In if (class(hourlydata) == "logical") { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
6: In projectRaster(dem, crs = crs(r)) : input and ouput crs are the same
7: In projectRaster(dem, crs = crs(r)) : input and ouput crs are the same
8: In projectRaster(dem, crs = crs(r)) : input and ouput crs are the same
9: In projectRaster(dem, crs = crs(r)) : input and ouput crs are the same

Did I miss something? Also, how is the ‘SatWater’ parameter accounted for in micro_ functions?

Thanks for the help!

Jonathan

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Setting up two types of layers in micro_ functions
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

Sorry, I forgot to fix the error checking code at the start of the functions, which was still assuming a single value. That's fixed now. What you ran would have worked but now there won't be warnings. The 'SatWater' parameter is internally computed but not relevant if the soil moisture model is running and soil moisture is not being provided as a given.

All the best,
Mike
